get.description:
Probe the SlimeRunner dispatcher via AMQP.

Returns a degraded shape (``reachable=False`` + ``error``) instead
of a 5xx so a polling client (Caddy / uptime-kuma / ops dashboard)
can keep its check generic.

Public knobs the registration form needs before it renders.

Always ``True`` once per-user invite codes ship: even if the operator
leaves ``settings.invite_codes`` empty (open global signup), an
existing user can still mint per-user codes that recipients redeem
on this same form. Keeping the field always-shown is the simplest
contract that supports both gates without forking the schema.

post.description:
Mint a reset token and email its raw value to the user.

Always returns 204 — even if the email isn't registered — so this
endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts. Vendor-side delivery
failures are logged + swallowed for the same reason.

Validate a reset token and rewrite the user's password.

Token must be: a SHA-256 hash that exists in ``password_reset_tokens``,
have ``used_at IS NULL``, and ``expires_at > now``. On success the
password is rewritten and the token is marked used.

Validate a verification token and mark the user's email verified.

Token must be: a SHA-256 hash that exists in
``email_verification_tokens``, have ``used_at IS NULL``, and
``expires_at > now``. On success ``users.email_verified_at`` is
stamped (idempotent — re-clicking a stale link returns 400, but a
user whose email is already verified is unaffected because the
token row flips ``used_at`` and won't match again).

Mirrors :func:`reset_password`'s error shape: one generic 400 for
every failure mode so an attacker can't tell "wrong token" from
"expired" from "already used". Returns the updated UserResponse so
the FE can immediately re-render without an extra ``/me`` round-
trip.

Re-mint and re-send the email-verification link for the signed-in user.

Authenticated-only — the FE banner is the entry point. Rate-limited
to 3/hour by the slowapi limiter so a leaked cookie can't burn the
SendGrid daily quota. No-ops with 204 if the user is already
verified (clicking "Resend" after verification is harmless and
we don't need to surface an error — the FE hides the banner once
``email_verified_at`` is set anyway).

Vendor delivery failures are logged + swallowed (same shape as
``/forgot``) so a transient SendGrid blip doesn't leak through to
the FE as a generic error; the user can retry.

patch.description:
Toggle whether a project shows in the caller's sidebar.

Per-user pin/unpin (ticket 020 — workspace IA v3 §2.4). Every
project is default-visible; this endpoint flips that for the caller
only — a shared project keeps independent visibility per recipient.
Hidden projects remain reachable via ``/app/projects``.

* ``hidden = True``  → upsert one row in
  ``project_visibility_overrides`` for ``(caller, project)``.
  Idempotent — re-issuing the call is a no-op (the row already
  exists). The endpoint also nudges ``updated_at`` on the existing
  row so audit / debugging can tell when the user last reasserted
  "hide this".
* ``hidden = False`` → DELETE any row for that pair so the project
  goes back to default-visible. Idempotent — DELETE on a missing
  row is a no-op.

The ownership gate piggybacks on ``_load_owned``: a 404 fires
when the project is not owned by the caller, matching the rest
of the router's permission story (a non-owner can't probe for
project-id existence by toggling visibility).

put.description:
Set / clear a project's recurring-scan schedule.

The four columns move together so the API is one PUT, not four
PATCHes:

* ``scan_schedule = "off"`` — clear everything (``scan_enabled =
  False``, ``scan_time = None``, ``next_scan = None``). The body's
  ``scan_time`` is ignored.
* ``scan_schedule`` recurring — require ``scan_time`` (Pydantic
  enforces), set ``scan_enabled = True``, and seed
  ``next_scan`` to the first firing instant strictly after now.

The sweep in ``scan_dispatcher.sweep_scheduled`` reads these
columns once a minute. We do not fire an immediate scan here —
the user gets the next-scheduled time as feedback, and the legacy
intel.surf form behaved the same way.

get.description:
Single-selector read.

Added so the Surf-detail page can mount the inline tag editor
without paging through the whole project's selector list. Returns
the same response shape as the list endpoints (tags + components
populated via the shared bulk loaders), keyed on ``selector_id``
ownership through the parent Project.

patch.description:
Patch one Selector — move between projects, set status, tag (v3 §9.2).

Every field is optional but at least one must be present (the
schema validator enforces this). ``project_id`` semantics:

* Field omitted        → no change.
* ``project_id: null`` → detach from current Project (move to
                         "unassigned").
* ``project_id: <int>`` → move under that Project. The caller
                          must own it (404 otherwise).

Tag mutations route through the same idempotent add/remove
plumbing as ``PATCH /api/selectors/{id}/tags`` — see that
endpoint's docstring for the full matrix.

get.description:
Return the most-recent JPEG screenshot for ``selector_id``.

Owner-scoped (same auth as the selector detail endpoints): a foreign
selector id 404s rather than leaking existence. Pulls the freshest
``rendered_pages`` row by ``id DESC`` — the renderer writes one row
per ``(selector, scan_job)`` pair, and re-scans overwrite the
matching pair, so picking the latest ``id`` lands on the freshly
captured snapshot.

Edge cases:

* No cached row OR the cached row carries a NULL ``screenshot_jpeg``
  (renderer ran but capture failed) → 404 with a clear detail.
  Returning an empty body would mislead clients that try to render
  the response as an image.

404.description: Selector not found, or no screenshot cached.

patch.description:
Per-selector tag add / remove (ticket 010).

The chips picker on the selectors table flows through this endpoint:
each ``[+]`` confirm sends ``add: [int|str]`` (existing id OR raw
name), each chip-X sends ``remove: [tag_id]``. The endpoint is
transactional — any ownership violation across ``add`` or ``remove``
fails the whole request with 403, no partial commit.

Behaviour matrix:

* ``add`` ints  — looked up under owner-scope; foreign / unknown
  id ⇒ 403.
* ``add`` strs  — normalised lowercase, idempotently upserted via
  the ``(owner_user_id, name)`` unique key from ticket 004.
* ``remove`` ints — must belong to the caller; foreign / unknown
  id ⇒ 403. An id that isn't currently on the selector is a no-op
  (still 200).

Returns the canonical ``SelectorResponse`` with ``tag_ids`` and
``tags`` populated so the FE renders the new chip set without a
second round-trip.

Bulk re-assign many Selectors to a Project in one transaction.

``project_id`` (workspace IA v3 §11) is the destination assignment
for every selector in ``selector_ids``. ``None`` moves the
Selectors to "unassigned" (the top-level "no project" bucket); a
non-NULL int moves them under that Project.

Ownership discipline (fail-closed): owner-scope every supplied id
against ``selectors.owner_user_id`` first; if the count differs
from the request length, every supplied id was NOT confirmed as
the caller's, and we 403 the whole request rather than silently
skip foreign rows. The single ``UPDATE`` that follows is
redundantly owner-scoped so a TOCTOU race can't sneak a foreign
row in between the check and the write.

The destination Project must also belong to the caller (404'd if
not). Wrapping the check + update in a single transaction means a
mid-flight failure rolls back atomically.

post.description:
Bulk-import selectors from a text-shaped upload (ticket 051).

Multipart upload of any of ``.txt`` / ``.csv`` / ``.tsv`` /
``.json`` / ``.html`` / ``.htm`` / ``.xml`` / ``.log``. The file is
read into memory (capped at ``settings.documents_max_bytes``),
regex-scanned by :mod:`app.services.url_extractor`, deduped against
the project's existing selectors, and the survivors are inserted as
a single transaction.

Edge cases:

* Empty file → 400 ``"Upload is empty"``.
* Unsupported extension → 400 with the allow-list.
* Oversize file → 413 with the MB cap.
* Project archived / foreign → 404 / 409 (mirrors the manual
  single-add path's ``_load_owned_project(require_active=True)``
  discipline).
* Zero URLs found in the file → 200 with ``imported=0,
  duplicates=0, invalid=0`` (the FE renders "no URLs found").
* Re-upload of the same file → 200 with ``imported=0`` and
  ``duplicates`` matching the prior import — no churn on the DB.

The ``imported_selectors`` field carries the freshly-inserted rows
so the FE can prepend them to the table without a follow-up
``GET /api/projects/{id}/selectors`` round-trip.

get.description:
Owner-scoped cross-project Selector list (v3 — workspace IA v3 §9.2).

Returns every Selector the caller owns, optionally filtered by
type / status / tag / project / unassigned-only, with server-side
pagination. Owner scoping reads ``Selector.owner_user_id`` so
unassigned rows are surfaced too.

post.description:
Run the user's prompt through the LLM extractor and return
validated selector candidates.

No auth requirement: the homepage hero form runs anonymously, so
the route accepts unauthenticated requests and the rate limiter
falls back to the IP key. The endpoint NEVER mutates state — it
returns candidates only; the FE routes confirmed candidates
through the regular selector-add path which has its own auth /
project-ownership gate.

The LLM call is synchronous (``llm.chat`` uses a sync httpx
client) so we wrap it in ``asyncio.to_thread`` to keep the event
loop unblocked.

Multipart upload of a single document under a project.

Returns 400 for unsupported extensions, 413 for oversize uploads.
On success the row lands at ``status=Uploaded`` and we fire-and-forget
``document_converter.convert.call_async`` so the worker picks it up
immediately. The worker's timer sweep is the safety net if AMQP is
down (the row stays in ``Uploaded`` and the next tick converts it).

Upsert one ``endpoint_agent_heartbeats`` row per (user, agent_id).

post.description:
Run the LLM extractor against a converted policy document.

Returns a list of validated proposals (possibly empty). NEVER
inserts into ``policy_rules`` — that's the accept endpoint
below. Returns 409 when the document hasn't been converted yet
so the FE can surface a friendly hint instead of a silent
empty list.

The per-document daily uniqueness cap means a re-call within
the same UTC day returns the cached proposal list (same UUIDs)
without burning another LLM call.

Insert one ``policy_rules`` row per accepted proposal.

Each item is re-validated against its ``rule_type``'s params
schema (so the FE can't sneak a bad payload past the
extractor's validation) and the originating document is
re-checked under the requesting user's ownership chain so a
forged ``source_document_id`` can't be slipped in.

Inserted rows carry ``source = 'extracted'`` and
``extracted_document_id = source_document_id``. Inserted rows
are returned as a flat ``PolicyRuleResponse`` list so the FE can
splice them directly into its rules table without a follow-up
GET.

All selectors must be owned by the caller and belong to the same project.
Each ScanJob is created with the same set of MicroserviceTasks. The

batch (each job stays Pending and can be re-fired).

post.description:
Public, unauthenticated scan submission from the homepage form.

Restores the legacy intel.surf "paste a domain, see a report"
top-of-funnel. Every submission is parented to a single synthetic
anon-owner project (lazy-seeded by
``app.anon.ensure_anon_owner_and_project``) so the existing
ScanJob → Selector → Project → User foreign-key chain still holds.

Hard guarantees:

* No auth — IP-keyed rate limit (``5/hour;20/day``) is the only
  throttle. ``user_or_ip_key`` would happily key on a stale cookie
  from someone else's signed-in tab; we explicitly use
  ``get_remote_address`` to keep the limit honest for true anon
  traffic.
* ``is_public`` is forced ``True`` and a slug is minted at create
  time. Anon submitters have no other way to reach their own scan
  since they don't have a session.
* The value is run through the same ``classify()`` detector the
  authenticated selector route uses, so ``host_from()`` / ``safe()``
  invariants downstream still hold. ``payload.selector_type`` is
  kept for parity with the old form but is not trusted.
* Tool list defaults to the scan_mode preset — quick runs the cheap
  subset; deep runs everything compatible with the selector type.
  Both modes honour the per-type compatibility filter so
  email_analyzer never fans out against an IP / Domain / FQDN / URL.

bookmarks alive and avoids slug recycling between unrelated scans.

``initial_label``) inline. The FE form is one round-trip: paste
your story, click submit, then click "Run analysis". Subsequent
artifacts go through the dedicated artifacts endpoint.

Validates that ``initial_body`` is paired with ``initial_kind``.
Analysis is intentionally NOT auto-dispatched -- the FE explicitly
calls ``/analyze`` so the user sees the report in ``open`` state
and can attach more artifacts before running synthesis.

get.description: Owner-scoped read. Returns the full report payload.

delete.description:
Owner-scoped delete. Cascades to artifacts / findings /
entities via the FK ``ON DELETE CASCADE``.

post.description:
Attach one artifact to the report.

Body length is validated by the schema layer; the report-level
guardrails (no public download routes, no auto-share) live on the
container row.

delete.description:
Owner-scoped delete of one artifact. Re-running ``analyze``
after a deletion is the expected path to refresh the synthesized
rows.

post.description:
Run one normalization pass on the report.

The synthesis call lives on the request hot-path so the FE gets
the rendered markdown body back in the POST response. The call
runs inside ``asyncio.to_thread`` against a sync session so the
FastAPI event loop stays responsive (mirrors
``scam_conversations.analyze_conversation``).

Turn the normalizer's suggested selectors into ``Selector`` rows.

Each entry is normalized via :func:`app.detect.classify` so the
final ``Selector`` row carries the canonical value + type.
Already-existing project selectors with the same value are
returned as-is (the FE renders the dedupe summary). Capped at the
schema limit (10 entries) so a runaway click can't fan out a huge
selector set.

Per the ticket safety guardrail, only domain / IP / URL / FQDN
selectors are accepted -- wallet / phone / bank-detail / name
entries are rejected with 400 even if the FE forwards them, so
the structured-evidence surface stays the only place those live.

Returns the list of ``Selector.id`` values (existing + freshly
created) so the FE can deep-link into the project's selector
panel and let the analyst kick off Surfs from there.

post.description:
Embed the user's query, cosine-rank against the user's OFIRs,
return the top-N hits with a short excerpt and risk score.

503 when the embeddings gateway is unconfigured / errored — the FE
surfaces the gateway-down message inline. Owner-scoped: cross-user
OFIRs are filtered out at the SQL boundary, not in Python.
