AbusePacketChecklistItem.title: AbusePacketChecklistItem
AbusePacketChecklistItem.description: One row in the analyst checklist.

AbusePacketCreateRequest.title: AbusePacketCreateRequest
AbusePacketCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/abuse-packets``.

All fields are validated server-side. ``recipient_type`` and
``tone`` use ``Literal`` so a bad value yields a 422 instead of
silently writing an unknown enum row. ``evidence_item_ids`` /
``evidence`` is the analyst's selected evidence; the router
rejects ids that are not owned by the same project.

``include_investigator_appendix`` defaults False per the safety
guardrail — analysts must explicitly opt in to including the
PII-bearing appendix.

AbusePacketEvidenceCreateRequest.title: AbusePacketEvidenceCreateRequest
AbusePacketEvidenceCreateRequest.description:
One evidence-attachment entry inside ``AbusePacketCreateRequest``.

``evidence_item_id`` references an ``EvidenceItem`` that already
exists in the same project (the router enforces project ownership
on every id). ``caption`` is an optional analyst-supplied label
that survives even if the underlying evidence row is later
deleted (the FK uses ``ondelete=SET NULL``).

AbusePacketEvidenceResponse.title: AbusePacketEvidenceResponse
AbusePacketEvidenceResponse.description:
One evidence row attached to a packet.

Carries the FK to the underlying ``EvidenceItem`` (may be NULL if
the analyst deleted the source evidence after the packet was
created) plus a hydrated snapshot (filename / sha256 / source
URL) so the FE can render the row without a follow-up GET.

AbusePacketResponse.title: AbusePacketResponse
AbusePacketResponse.description:
Full abuse-packet shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

Joins the parent packet row with its recipient + evidence rows
and the deserialized JSON sidecars (safe redactions and analyst
checklist).

AbusePacketSafeRedaction.title: AbusePacketSafeRedaction
AbusePacketSafeRedaction.description:
One redaction the generator flagged as recommended.

Mirrors the shape produced by ``evidence_redactor.prefilled_redactions``
so the FE can render a single redactions table whether the source
is the packet generator or the redactor service.

AbusePacketSummaryResponse.title: AbusePacketSummaryResponse
AbusePacketSummaryResponse.description:
One row in the per-project abuse-packet listing.

Carries enough context to render the table without expanding each
row (recipient kind, status chip, evidence count, generation
timestamp).

AbusePacketUpdateRequest.title: AbusePacketUpdateRequest
AbusePacketUpdateRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/projects/{pid}/abuse-packets/{packet_id}``.

Every field is optional so analysts can tweak one knob without
re-sending the whole packet. Re-running ``generate`` after a
tweak refreshes the packet body to reflect the new inputs.

AliasAnalysisRunDetailResponse.title: AliasAnalysisRunDetailResponse
AliasAnalysisRunDetailResponse.description: Run row + the hypotheses it produced (in confidence-desc order).

AliasEvidenceCreateRequest.title: AliasEvidenceCreateRequest
AliasEvidenceCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/alias-subjects/{sid}/evidence``.

Per the ticket's "require user to affirm uploaded evidence is
lawful to process" guardrail, ``lawful_processing_affirmed`` must
be ``True``. The router rejects rows that don't carry the
affirmation with a 400.

AliasEvidenceResponse.title: AliasEvidenceResponse
AliasEvidenceResponse.description: One evidence snippet row attached to a subject.

AliasHypothesisCitation.title: AliasHypothesisCitation
AliasHypothesisCitation.description:
One citation pointing at an identifier or evidence row.

The deconflictor emits one entry per supporting signal so the FE
can render evidence-backed hypotheses without re-resolving by id.

AliasHypothesisDecisionRequest.title: AliasHypothesisDecisionRequest
AliasHypothesisDecisionRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/alias-hypotheses/{hid}/decision``.

``approve`` and ``reject`` are the only accepted actions; the
decision flips ``status`` and stamps ``decided_at`` atomically.
Re-deciding (e.g. flipping rejected → approved) is allowed so
analysts can revise a call after new evidence.

AliasIdentifierResponse.title: AliasIdentifierResponse
AliasIdentifierResponse.description: One identifier row attached to a subject.

AliasLinkHypothesisResponse.title: AliasLinkHypothesisResponse
AliasLinkHypothesisResponse.description: One proposed link between two subjects.

AliasSubjectCreateRequest.title: AliasSubjectCreateRequest
AliasSubjectCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/alias-subjects``.

``label`` is required and bounded so the workspace renders cleanly
in a table. Identifiers + evidence are added via separate endpoints
so the body shape stays predictable.

AliasSubjectDetailResponse.title: AliasSubjectDetailResponse
AliasSubjectDetailResponse.description: Full subject shape with identifiers + evidence.

AliasWorkspaceResponse.title: AliasWorkspaceResponse
AliasWorkspaceResponse.description:
Aggregate workspace payload returned by the GET-list endpoint.

A single fetch carries everything the alias workspace renders so
a fresh F5 page load doesn't have to fan out across CRUD endpoints.

AnonymousScanCreate.title: AnonymousScanCreate
AnonymousScanCreate.description:
Payload for ``POST /api/scan-jobs/anonymous``.

``selector_type`` is informational — the legacy intel.surf form lets
users pick ``AutoDetect``/``IP``/``Root Domain Name``/``FQDN``/``URL``,
but the actual sanitisation runs through ``app.detect.classify`` which
re-derives the type from the value. We accept the field for parity but
don't trust it.

AnonymousScanResponse.title: AnonymousScanResponse
AnonymousScanResponse.description:
Slim response — the caller has no auth, so we only return the bits
they need to reach the public scan view: the slug and the resolved
selector value (so the FE can echo what was just submitted).

ApiKeyCreatedResponse.title: ApiKeyCreatedResponse
ApiKeyCreatedResponse.description: Returned ONCE on creation. ``secret`` is the only chance to see it.

ApiKeyResponse.title: ApiKeyResponse
ApiKeyResponse.description: List/revoke response — never includes the plaintext secret.

BecAnalysisResponse.title: BecAnalysisResponse
BecAnalysisResponse.description: One analysis row for a case (the synthesized brief + bookkeeping).

BecArtifactCreateRequest.title: BecArtifactCreateRequest
BecArtifactCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/bec-cases/{cid}/artifacts``.

``kind`` selects the parser branch; ``label`` is an optional
human-readable name (defaults to "(no label)" when omitted);
``body`` is the verbatim artifact text. Length cap mirrors the
``Selector`` validator for the email-headers path so analysts can
paste the same blob into either feature.

BecArtifactResponse.title: BecArtifactResponse
BecArtifactResponse.description: One artifact row attached to a case.

BecCaseCreateRequest.title: BecCaseCreateRequest
BecCaseCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/bec-cases``.

``title`` is required and bounded so the case list view stays
scannable. Artifacts are uploaded via a separate endpoint (one
artifact per request) so the body shape stays predictable.

BecCaseDetailResponse.title: BecCaseDetailResponse
BecCaseDetailResponse.description:
Full case shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

Includes every artifact, every entity, every payment step, and
the full latest-analysis row so a fresh F5 page load renders the
case without a follow-up call.

BecCaseSummaryResponse.title: BecCaseSummaryResponse
BecCaseSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project case list.

BecEntityResponse.title: BecEntityResponse
BecEntityResponse.description:
One synthesized entity row.

``kind`` is the discriminator the FE keys table grouping on
(sender / recipient / lookalike_domain / iban / account / ...).

BecPaymentStepResponse.title: BecPaymentStepResponse
BecPaymentStepResponse.description: One row in the reconstructed payment-redirection chain.

BecRunSelectedSelectorsRequest.title: BecRunSelectedSelectorsRequest
BecRunSelectedSelectorsRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/bec-cases/{cid}/run-selectors``.

Sends the suggested selectors the analyst ticked back into the
project's normal selector pipeline. The router creates one
``Selector`` per entry (deduped against the project's existing
selectors) and dispatches one Surf each. Capped at 10 entries to
bound the per-click ScanJob fan-out; matches the synthesizer's
own ``_MAX_SUGGESTED_SELECTORS``.

BecSuggestedSelector.title: BecSuggestedSelector
BecSuggestedSelector.description:
One Surf candidate the analyzer recommends.

Mirrors :class:`SelectorCreate`'s shape so the FE can post the
candidates straight into the existing selector-creation endpoint
without a translation layer.

BrandHuntChildResponse.title: BrandHuntChildResponse
BrandHuntChildResponse.description:
One child Surf row inside a brand-hunt detail response.

Mirrors the smallest subset of ``ScanJobResponse`` the brand-hunt
UI needs to render the per-candidate row: the candidate domain,
its current status, and the AI risk score (so the FE can sort the
table by risk descending).

BrandHuntCreateRequest.title: BrandHuntCreateRequest
BrandHuntCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/brand-hunts``.

The brand domain is whatever the analyst typed — we run it through
``app.detect.classify`` server-side to enforce the Domain / FQDN
shape and reject anything else (URLs, IPs, garbage). Length cap
matches ``Selector.value`` since we re-use the same column shape
for child selectors.

BrandHuntDetailResponse.title: BrandHuntDetailResponse
BrandHuntDetailResponse.description:
Returned by ``GET /api/projects/{pid}/brand-hunts/{id}``.

The ``summary_markdown`` field is populated only after every child
Surf has hit a terminal status AND the meta-summary LLM call has
completed. Until then the FE polls and renders per-candidate rows.

BrandHuntStartResponse.title: BrandHuntStartResponse
BrandHuntStartResponse.description:
Returned by ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/brand-hunts``.

``candidates`` echoes the validated candidate list so the UI can
render the per-candidate rows immediately. ``surfed_count`` may be
smaller than ``candidate_count`` when monthly Surf quota was the
constraint; ``skipped_for_quota`` is the difference, surfaced so
the UI can show a "capped at N" hint.

BrandHuntSummaryResponse.title: BrandHuntSummaryResponse
BrandHuntSummaryResponse.description:
One row in the ``GET /api/projects/{pid}/brand-hunts`` list.

Lighter than ``BrandHuntDetailResponse`` (no children, no
summary_markdown) so the project-scoped listing endpoint stays
cheap.

CaseSimilarityMatchResponse.title: CaseSimilarityMatchResponse
CaseSimilarityMatchResponse.description:
One row in a similarity run's match list.

The matched project's name is filled in by the router from the
same-user project lookup. By construction (the matcher only ever
persists rows for projects owned by the requesting user), this
cannot leak another user's project name into the response.

CaseSimilarityRunDetailResponse.title: CaseSimilarityRunDetailResponse
CaseSimilarityRunDetailResponse.description: Full payload returned by ``POST .../run`` and the per-run GET.

CaseSimilarityRunRequest.title: CaseSimilarityRunRequest
CaseSimilarityRunRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/similar-cases/run``.

Currently empty — the matcher always rebuilds the target's
fingerprint and compares against every fingerprint owned by the
same user. Reserved for future opt-in cross-organization knobs
(which will get their own ticket per the spec).

CaseSimilarityWorkspaceResponse.title: CaseSimilarityWorkspaceResponse
CaseSimilarityWorkspaceResponse.description:
Full payload returned by the workspace GET.

``latest_run`` is ``None`` when the project has never been
matched; the FE renders an empty-state with a "Find similar cases"
button in that case.

ChatMessageCreate.title: ChatMessageCreate
ChatMessageCreate.description:
Payload for ``POST /api/scan-jobs/{id}/chat``.

Length cap is generous (4k chars ≈ a paragraph or two) but bounded
so a runaway client can't post a multi-megabyte prompt; the service
layer truncates again as a defensive belt-and-braces.

ChatMessageRead.title: ChatMessageRead
ChatMessageRead.description:
One row in the message history.

``model_used`` / ``prompt_tokens`` / ``completion_tokens`` are
populated only for assistant rows; user rows leave them ``None``.

CopilotMessageRead.title: CopilotMessageRead
CopilotMessageRead.description:
One row in a session transcript.

``tool_name`` / ``tool_args_json`` are populated only on
assistant rows that called a tool AND on the matching tool result
row. ``model_used`` / ``prompt_tokens`` / ``completion_tokens``
are populated only on assistant rows. The FE renders tool rows
with a compact "ran X with args" pill so the analyst can audit
every tool call.

CopilotSessionCreate.title: CopilotSessionCreate
CopilotSessionCreate.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/copilot/sessions``.

``title`` is optional — the service auto-titles a session from
the first user message when this is omitted, mirroring the
ChatGPT / Claude UI pattern.

CopilotSessionDetail.title: CopilotSessionDetail
CopilotSessionDetail.description:
Full session shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

Includes the message history so a fresh client load (or an
F5 refresh) renders the full transcript without a second call.

CopilotSessionRead.title: CopilotSessionRead
CopilotSessionRead.description: One row in the session list (no message history).

CopilotStepRequest.title: CopilotStepRequest
CopilotStepRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/copilot/sessions/{sid}/step``.

Length cap is generous (4 KB ≈ a paragraph or two) but bounded so
a runaway client can't post a multi-megabyte prompt; the service
layer truncates again as a defensive belt-and-braces.

CopilotStepResponse.title: CopilotStepResponse
CopilotStepResponse.description:
The assistant + tool rows freshly appended by one step call.

The FE diffs the returned list against its current transcript so
a client always renders the same shape regardless of whether the
agent loop ran 0, 1, 2, or 3 tool calls in this turn.

CryptoTraceArtifactCreateRequest.title: CryptoTraceArtifactCreateRequest
CryptoTraceArtifactCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/crypto-traces/{rid}/artifacts``.

``kind`` selects the parser branch; ``chain`` is an optional
analyst hint that the parser uses as the default when the
artifact body itself doesn't carry a chain column. ``label`` is
a short human-readable name (defaults to "(no label)" when
omitted); ``body`` is the verbatim artifact text. Length cap is
256 KB to allow real-world block-explorer CSV exports.

The wallet-address and transaction-hash kinds carry a *single*
value as the body so the synthesizer can render them cleanly in
the appendix. Validation against the chain regexes lives on the
router, not here — the schema only enforces shape.

CryptoTraceFreezeTarget.title: CryptoTraceFreezeTarget
CryptoTraceFreezeTarget.description:
One freeze / preservation-request candidate.

The synthesizer's LLM emits these in a trailing JSON block; the
FE renders them as a checklist next to the packet markdown.

CryptoTraceRequestCreateRequest.title: CryptoTraceRequestCreateRequest
CryptoTraceRequestCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/crypto-traces``.

``title`` is required and bounded so the listing view stays
scannable. ``primary_chain`` is optional — when set, the
synthesizer prefers it over per-artifact auto-detection.

CryptoTraceRequestDetailResponse.title: CryptoTraceRequestDetailResponse
CryptoTraceRequestDetailResponse.description: Full crypto-trace shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

CryptoTraceRequestSummaryResponse.title: CryptoTraceRequestSummaryResponse
CryptoTraceRequestSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project crypto-trace request listing.

arg.title: Arg
arg.description: Integer id of the target row to dispatch against.

DocumentResponse.title: DocumentResponse
DocumentResponse.description:
List/detail response for a project document.

``markdown_content`` is included so the detail view can render the
converted markdown without a second round-trip. The list view ignores
it client-side; SQLite is fine returning the column on listings since
the upper bound (10 MB original) is well within typical row budgets,
and we read at most ~50 rows per project.

EndpointAgentLogResponse.title: EndpointAgentLogResponse
EndpointAgentLogResponse.description: One row as the Early Detection page consumes it.

EndpointAgentSummary.title: EndpointAgentSummary
EndpointAgentSummary.description:
One enrolled endpoint, as the "Endpoints" panel renders it.

``last_seen_at`` is ``max(last_heartbeat_at, last_event_at)`` — i.e.
"most recent sign of life of any kind". The client uses this to
render the Online / Idle / Offline badge so the threshold can be
tuned without a deploy.

EvidenceCustodyEventCreateRequest.title: EvidenceCustodyEventCreateRequest
EvidenceCustodyEventCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/evidence/{eid}/custody``.

The append-only timeline is the analyst's audit ledger; the only
free-form custody event the FE can post is a ``note`` (with the
note text on the row). Other event types (``uploaded`` /
``redaction_*`` / ``packet_generated``) are written by the
corresponding action routes — they don't need a manual surface.

EvidenceCustodyEventResponse.title: EvidenceCustodyEventResponse
EvidenceCustodyEventResponse.description: One row in the append-only custody timeline.

EvidenceEntityResponse.title: EvidenceEntityResponse
EvidenceEntityResponse.description: One node in a project's evidence entity graph.

EvidenceGraphResponse.title: EvidenceGraphResponse
EvidenceGraphResponse.description:
Full graph payload returned by ``GET /api/projects/{pid}/evidence-graph``.

``latest_run`` is ``None`` when the project has never been built —
the FE renders a "Build graph" empty state in that case.

EvidenceItemCreateRequest.title: EvidenceItemCreateRequest
EvidenceItemCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/evidence``.

The body is paste-text v1 (the same shape the BEC analyzer
accepts). ``original_filename`` and ``content_type`` pin the
deterministic provenance fields the chain-of-custody timeline
cites. ``source_url`` and ``notes`` are optional analyst metadata.

EvidenceItemDetailResponse.title: EvidenceItemDetailResponse
EvidenceItemDetailResponse.description:
Full evidence-item shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

Includes every version, every custody event, every redaction,
and every packet so a fresh F5 page load renders the vault page
without follow-up calls.

EvidenceItemSummaryResponse.title: EvidenceItemSummaryResponse
EvidenceItemSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project evidence-vault list.

EvidenceItemVersionResponse.title: EvidenceItemVersionResponse
EvidenceItemVersionResponse.description: One immutable version of an evidence item's body.

EvidenceProposedRedaction.title: EvidenceProposedRedaction
EvidenceProposedRedaction.description:
One AI-flagged span the redactor wants to redact.

``category`` is a short discriminator (``email`` / ``phone`` /
``ssn`` / ``credit_card`` / ``iban`` / ``ip`` / ``custom``) so
the analyst can scan the proposals quickly. ``original`` carries
the verbatim text the AI saw; ``replacement`` is what the AI
suggests redacting it to (typically ``[REDACTED-EMAIL]`` etc.).

EvidenceRedactionResponse.title: EvidenceRedactionResponse
EvidenceRedactionResponse.description: One AI-proposed redaction draft awaiting human approval.

EvidenceRelationResponse.title: EvidenceRelationResponse
EvidenceRelationResponse.description:
One edge between two ``EvidenceEntity`` rows.

The FE renders ``origin='ai'`` rows with a "hypothesis" badge per
the ticket guardrails. ``evidence_markdown`` is the citation /
rationale the analyst sees on edge click.

EvidenceSharePacketCreateRequest.title: EvidenceSharePacketCreateRequest
EvidenceSharePacketCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/evidence/{eid}/packets``.

``audience`` selects the recipient class so the redactor can tune
wording (a victim packet reads differently from a law-enforcement
packet). The route uses the latest approved redaction's
``partner_packet_text`` as the packet body when one exists, and
falls back to the original body wrapped in a "no redaction
approved yet" warning otherwise.

EvidenceSharePacketResponse.title: EvidenceSharePacketResponse
EvidenceSharePacketResponse.description: One curated share packet for an evidence item.

ExtortionAffectedDataItem.title: ExtortionAffectedDataItem
ExtortionAffectedDataItem.description: One affected-data-category row in the dossier.

ExtortionArtifactCreateRequest.title: ExtortionArtifactCreateRequest
ExtortionArtifactCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/extortion-cases/{cid}/artifacts``.

``kind`` selects how the synthesizer renders the body in the
prompt; ``label`` is a short human-readable tag (defaults to
"(no label)" when omitted); ``body`` is the verbatim artifact
text. Length cap is 256 KB to allow real-world ransom-note
dumps and file-tree paste-ins.

The router computes the SHA-256 ``source_hash`` server-side; it
is not part of the request body so a buggy client cannot poison
the audit anchor.

ExtortionCaseCreateRequest.title: ExtortionCaseCreateRequest
ExtortionCaseCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/extortion-cases``.

``title`` is required and bounded so the listing view stays
scannable. ``suspected_actor_hint`` and ``incident_started_at``
are optional analyst metadata — when supplied the synthesizer
seeds the prompt with them but always tags the actor as
"claimed" / "suspected" until the artifact text supports a
stronger qualifier.

ExtortionCaseDetailResponse.title: ExtortionCaseDetailResponse
ExtortionCaseDetailResponse.description: Full extortion-case shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

ExtortionCaseSummaryResponse.title: ExtortionCaseSummaryResponse
ExtortionCaseSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project extortion-case listing.

ExtortionIndicatorPromoteResponse.title: ExtortionIndicatorPromoteResponse
ExtortionIndicatorPromoteResponse.description:
Returned by the indicator-promotion endpoint.

The indicator row gains ``becomes_selector=True`` and a fresh
project ``Selector`` row is inserted (or returned, if one
already exists with the same value). ``selector_id`` is the
id the FE can navigate to.

ExtortionRansomDemand.title: ExtortionRansomDemand
ExtortionRansomDemand.description:
One ransom-demand block extracted by the synthesizer.

The LLM emits one such block in the trailing ``# ransom_demand``
JSON fence. Empty / unknown values are returned as empty strings
so the FE can render a single panel without optional fields
going missing in the JSON.

ExtractedIocs.title: ExtractedIocs
ExtractedIocs.description:
Validated bag of IOCs returned by the extraction step.

Every entry has already passed ``app.detect.classify`` for the
Surfable categories (``ips`` / ``domains`` / ``urls``). Hashes and
emails are recorded for the UI but no Surf is fanned out for them
in v1 (no hash / email enrichment tool ships yet).

ForgotPasswordRequest.title: ForgotPasswordRequest
ForgotPasswordRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/auth/forgot``.

The endpoint always returns 204, so a malformed body is the only path
that surfaces a 4xx — and even there the response body must not leak
whether the email was registered.

HeartbeatRequest.title: HeartbeatRequest
HeartbeatRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /api/early-detection/heartbeat``.

Both fields are optional so a quiet agent can still ping with just
its identity. The server falls back to ``"unknown"`` for ``agent_id``
on agents that have not picked a hostname yet, so every heartbeat
yields exactly one upsert row.

LeakEntityResponse.title: LeakEntityResponse
LeakEntityResponse.description: One synthesized entity row attached to a listing.

LeakListingDetailResponse.title: LeakListingDetailResponse
LeakListingDetailResponse.description:
Listing + its entities + relevance findings.

Used by ``GET /api/projects/{pid}/leak-listings/{lid}`` so the FE
can render the listing-detail panel without a fan-out call.

LeakListingResponse.title: LeakListingResponse
LeakListingResponse.description: One parsed listing row (summary shape, no children).

LeakRelevanceFindingResponse.title: LeakRelevanceFindingResponse
LeakRelevanceFindingResponse.description: One scored relevance finding linking a listing to a project signal.

LeakSourceCreateRequest.title: LeakSourceCreateRequest
LeakSourceCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/leak-sources``.

Either ``url`` (URL kinds) or ``body`` (body kinds) must be set.
Mixing — passing both — is rejected by the validator below to
keep the source row's intent unambiguous (URL vs static body).

``watch_terms`` is an optional per-source list of free-text
keywords the relevance pass should match against in addition to
project selectors / brand terms.

LeakSourceDetailResponse.title: LeakSourceDetailResponse
LeakSourceDetailResponse.description:
Full source shape: settings + recent runs + recent listings.

Returned by ``GET /api/projects/{pid}/leak-sources/{sid}``. The
listings list is capped (newest-first) so a hot source doesn't
return megabytes of body text on a F5; the FE pages through
``GET .../listings`` for older entries.

LeakSourceSummaryResponse.title: LeakSourceSummaryResponse
LeakSourceSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project source list.

LeakSourceUpdateRequest.title: LeakSourceUpdateRequest
LeakSourceUpdateRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/projects/{pid}/leak-sources/{sid}``.

All fields are optional; only those supplied are updated. The
``source_type`` is intentionally immutable post-create — changing
it would invalidate every prior listing's parse / dedupe history.

LegalReturnArtifactCreateRequest.title: LegalReturnArtifactCreateRequest
LegalReturnArtifactCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/legal-returns/{iid}/artifacts``.

``document_id`` references an already-uploaded ``Document`` row in
the same project (the analyst uploads via the existing Documents
surface, then attaches it here). ``label`` is an optional analyst
note ("Bank-of-X subscriber records"); falls back to the
document's ``original_filename`` when omitted.

LegalReturnArtifactResponse.title: LegalReturnArtifactResponse
LegalReturnArtifactResponse.description: One artifact row attached to an import.

LegalReturnEntityResponse.title: LegalReturnEntityResponse
LegalReturnEntityResponse.description:
One synthesized entity row.

``selector_eligible`` is the FE's "create selector" checkbox guard:
only network-classifiable kinds (email / IP / domain / URL) are
safe to convert into project ``Selector`` rows. Sensitive
subscriber details stay evidence-only.

LegalReturnExtractionResponse.title: LegalReturnExtractionResponse
LegalReturnExtractionResponse.description: One persisted extraction row (the synthesized summary + bookkeeping).

LegalReturnImportCreateRequest.title: LegalReturnImportCreateRequest
LegalReturnImportCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/legal-returns``.

``title`` is required and bounded so the imports list view stays
scannable. ``provider`` is the chip the FE renders + a hint to
the parser about what shape to expect. Artifacts are attached
via a separate endpoint (one document per request) so the body
shape stays predictable.

LegalReturnImportDetailResponse.title: LegalReturnImportDetailResponse
LegalReturnImportDetailResponse.description:
Full import shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

Includes every artifact, every entity, and the latest extraction
so a fresh F5 page load renders the import without a follow-up call.

LegalReturnImportSummaryResponse.title: LegalReturnImportSummaryResponse
LegalReturnImportSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project imports list.

LegalReturnImportUpdateRequest.title: LegalReturnImportUpdateRequest
LegalReturnImportUpdateRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/projects/{pid}/legal-returns/{iid}``.

Each field is optional — the FE sends only the keys the analyst
edited. ``status`` is intentionally read-only; the parser flips
it via the analyze route.

LegalReturnRunSelectorsRequest.title: LegalReturnRunSelectorsRequest
LegalReturnRunSelectorsRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/legal-returns/{iid}/run-selectors``.

Capped at 25 entries to bound the per-click ``Selector`` fan-out
(a return can carry hundreds of IPs / emails; the analyst
explicitly picks which ones become selectors).

LegalReturnSelectorCandidate.title: LegalReturnSelectorCandidate
LegalReturnSelectorCandidate.description:
One candidate selector the analyst ticks before "Create selectors".

Mirrors :class:`SelectorCreate` so the router can post the
candidates straight into the existing classifier without a
translation layer.

LegalReturnTimelineEntry.title: LegalReturnTimelineEntry
LegalReturnTimelineEntry.description: One row in the normalized timeline.

LogIngestBatch.title: LogIngestBatch
LogIngestBatch.description: A batch shipped by one agent at one moment in time.

LogIngestEntry.title: LogIngestEntry
LogIngestEntry.description:
One webserver-honeypot request as the agent saw it.

Mirrors the JSONL shape that ``rroger.webserver.RequestLogger`` writes
to ``~/.rroger/webserver/requests-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl``.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: Seconds before the tool is killed; omit for the tool default.

ManualToolRunResponse.title: ManualToolRunResponse
ManualToolRunResponse.description: Result envelope returned by a manual tool run.

ManualToolSummary.title: ManualToolSummary
ManualToolSummary.description: One scan-tool descriptor surfaced in the logged-in Tools section.

MediaEvidenceAnalysisResponse.title: MediaEvidenceAnalysisResponse
MediaEvidenceAnalysisResponse.description:
One persisted analysis row for a media evidence artifact.

``metadata_json`` is the deterministic parser output (extension,
sniffed magic bytes, mismatch flags). It's always populated, even
in degraded-AI mode. ``summary_markdown`` is the analyst-facing
brief; in degraded mode it's a placeholder explaining why AI
synthesis is off and what was preserved.

MediaEvidenceDetailResponse.title: MediaEvidenceDetailResponse
MediaEvidenceDetailResponse.description:
Full media-evidence shape returned by GET-by-id.

Includes the analyst paste-text fields, the freshly-rendered
indicators list, and the latest analysis row so a fresh F5 page
load renders the artifact in one round-trip.

MediaEvidenceIndicatorResponse.title: MediaEvidenceIndicatorResponse
MediaEvidenceIndicatorResponse.description:
One indicator-to-review for a media evidence row.

``source`` separates parser-derived rows (deterministic
metadata observations) from ``ai`` rows (AI-synthesized
impressions). The FE renders the two groups distinctly so the
analyst never confuses a heuristic for a forensic finding.

MediaEvidenceSummaryResponse.title: MediaEvidenceSummaryResponse
MediaEvidenceSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project media evidence list.

MediaEvidenceUpdateRequest.title: MediaEvidenceUpdateRequest
MediaEvidenceUpdateRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/media-evidence/{id}``.

Only the analyst-editable paste-text fields can be modified. The
immutable provenance columns (hash, byte size, original filename,
content type, media type, status) are read-only — chain-of-custody
requires they survive the lifetime of the artifact.

outputs_path.title: Outputs Path
outputs_path.description: Path of the outputs JSON file inside the job dir.

MicroserviceRunResponse.title: MicroserviceRunResponse
MicroserviceRunResponse.description:
Observability row for one microservice @rpc invocation.

Surfaced inside ``ScanJobResponse.microservice_runs`` so the owner
view can render a per-microservice timing table. ``inputs_path`` and
``outputs_path`` are deliberately omitted — they hold absolute
container paths (``/opt/surfSelectors/<job>/...``) that would leak
operator infrastructure if rendered to the page.

job_uuid.title: Job Uuid
job_uuid.description: The owning scan job's UUID. NULL for ad-hoc runs.

parent_microservice.title: Parent Microservice
parent_microservice.description: Set when this run was triggered by cross_service @rpc.

inputs_path.title: Inputs Path
inputs_path.description: Path of the inputs JSON file inside the job dir.

MicroserviceStartedRequest.title: MicroserviceStartedRequest
MicroserviceStartedRequest.description:
Pre-hook payload posted by ``intelsurf_shared.microservice_lifecycle``.

Records that a Nameko @rpc invocation has begun. Idempotent on
``(job_uuid, microservice_name, started_at)``.

PivotResponse.title: PivotResponse
PivotResponse.description:
One pivot suggestion as returned by ``GET /api/scan-jobs/{id}/pivots``.

The persisted JSON array is already normalized server-side
(``app.services.report_generator._normalize_pivots``): selectors
pass ``detect.classify``, types are detector-canonical, confidence
is clamped to ``[0, 1]``, rationale is length-capped. The schema
here is a light, defensive read-side projection so a corrupt row
can't 500 the listing.

PivotRunResponse.title: PivotRunResponse
PivotRunResponse.description:
Returned by ``POST /api/scan-jobs/{id}/pivots/{idx}/run`` after a
new follow-up Surf has been kicked off.

The FE uses ``scan_job_id`` to navigate the user to the freshly
created ScanJob view.

PolicyFindingResponse.title: PolicyFindingResponse
PolicyFindingResponse.description:
Joined read-side projection of one ``PolicyFinding`` row.

The router populates the joined ``rule_*`` fields from
``PolicyRule`` so the FE never has to issue a second round-trip to
render the Compliance section. Both joined fields are optional —
``policy_rule_id`` is ``SET NULL`` on rule delete, in which case
the finding is still useful as a historical record but renders
with a "(rule deleted)" placeholder.

PolicyProposalAcceptItem.title: PolicyProposalAcceptItem
PolicyProposalAcceptItem.description:
One proposal the user is accepting from the review dialog.

The client echoes the original ``proposal_id`` back so the audit
log can correlate accepts with the source extraction call.
``params`` / ``description`` may be edited from the originally
proposed values — both are re-validated server-side against the
rule_type's params schema and the description length cap.

PolicyProposalResponse.title: PolicyProposalResponse
PolicyProposalResponse.description:
One LLM-extracted policy-rule proposal returned for review.

The ``proposal_id`` is a transient UUID minted server-side per
extraction call. The FE includes proposals it wants to keep in
the accept call, optionally editing ``params`` / ``description``
along the way. The shape mirrors the ``ProposedRule`` dataclass in
:mod:`app.services.policy_rule_extractor` so the router can do a
flat ``model_validate(p.to_dict())`` projection.

PolicyProposalsAcceptRequest.title: PolicyProposalsAcceptRequest
PolicyProposalsAcceptRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/policy-rules/from-proposals``.

The FE sends back exactly the proposals the user toggled
"Accept" on. The server inserts one ``policy_rules`` row per
proposal, sets ``source = 'extracted'``, and populates
``extracted_document_id`` with ``source_document_id``.

PolicyProposalsAcceptResponse.title: PolicyProposalsAcceptResponse
PolicyProposalsAcceptResponse.description:
Returned after the accept call inserts the surviving rules.

``rules`` is the list of inserted ``PolicyRuleResponse`` rows so
the FE can splice them straight into its rules table without a
follow-up GET.

PolicyProposalsResponse.title: PolicyProposalsResponse
PolicyProposalsResponse.description:
Returned by ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/documents/{did}/propose-rules``.

``proposals`` is the validated proposal list (possibly empty —
the FE renders the empty state when no proposals survived). The
``degraded_reason`` field is non-empty when the extractor
couldn't run end-to-end (LLM unconfigured, malformed model
output, etc.) so the FE can surface a friendly hint instead of
a silent empty list.

PolicyRuleCreate.title: PolicyRuleCreate
PolicyRuleCreate.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/policy-rules``.

For v1 the only ``rule_type`` is ``port_must_not_be_public`` and
``params`` must match :class:`PortMustNotBePublicParams`. The router
validates and re-serializes ``params`` to the persisted JSON string
so the DB column stays canonical.

PolicyRuleUpdate.title: PolicyRuleUpdate
PolicyRuleUpdate.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/policy-rules/{rid}``.

Every field is optional — callers send only what they want to
change. ``params`` is re-validated against the rule's current
``rule_type`` server-side; we don't allow ``rule_type`` to be
changed once persisted (different evaluator semantics, no useful
migration story for in-flight findings).

PortScanOpenPortsResponse.title: PortScanOpenPortsResponse
PortScanOpenPortsResponse.description:
Response body for ``GET /api/internal/scan-jobs/{job_id}/port-scan/{target}/open-ports``.

Consumed by MS84_TracerouteTcpPorts to decide which TCP port to
traceroute against. ``open_ports`` is sorted ascending so the
caller's priority-pick (443 > 80 > 22 > min remaining) is stable
across reruns.

ProjectBriefCreateRequest.title: ProjectBriefCreateRequest
ProjectBriefCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/briefs``.

Both fields are optional. When ``scan_job_ids`` is omitted the
service defaults to "the most recent Complete ScanJob per
selector in the project, capped at 50". An explicit list lets
the caller scope the brief to a specific subset (e.g. "brief
these 5 selectors only" from a multi-selector picker UI).

The list is capped at 200 entries at the validator boundary —
bigger than the service-side ``DEFAULT_MAX_SCAN_JOBS`` (50) so
the truncation logic still gets exercised when a caller passes
too many ids; small enough that a runaway client can't post a
multi-megabyte JSON array to chew the LLM budget.

ProjectBriefDetailResponse.title: ProjectBriefDetailResponse
ProjectBriefDetailResponse.description:
Full payload returned by ``GET /api/projects/{pid}/briefs/{id}``.

Adds the synthesized markdown body, the LLM token bookkeeping,
and the explicit ``included_scan_job_ids`` array so the FE can
render "this brief stitched these N Surfs" with deep links.

ProjectBriefSummaryResponse.title: ProjectBriefSummaryResponse
ProjectBriefSummaryResponse.description:
One row in the ``GET /api/projects/{pid}/briefs`` listing.

Slim — no markdown body, no included ScanJob list. The "Briefs"
card on the project page only needs enough to render the row
(risk chip, model, timestamps); full body lives behind the
detail GET.

ProjectScheduleResponse.title: ProjectScheduleResponse
ProjectScheduleResponse.description:
Read-side projection of the four schedule columns.

Embedded in ``ProjectResponse`` so the FE can show the current
schedule + the next firing instant after a save without re-fetching.

ProjectScheduleUpdate.title: ProjectScheduleUpdate
ProjectScheduleUpdate.description:
Body for ``PUT /api/projects/{id}/schedule``.

The four columns move together: ``scan_schedule == "off"`` clears
everything regardless of the other fields, and any recurring value
requires ``scan_time``. We validate that pairing here so the router
does not have to repeat it.

ProjectVisibilityUpdate.title: ProjectVisibilityUpdate
ProjectVisibilityUpdate.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/projects/{project_id}/visibility`` (ticket 020).

Per-user sidebar pin/unpin (workspace IA v3 §2.4). ``hidden = True``
upserts a ``project_visibility_overrides`` row for ``(caller, project)``;
``hidden = False`` DELETEs any existing row so the project goes back
to default-visible. Both branches are idempotent; the endpoint
returns 204 either way.

PublicScanDetail.title: PublicScanDetail
PublicScanDetail.description:
The slug-keyed public report payload.

Mirrors the owner-facing ScanJobResponse shape minus owner identifiers
(``project_id``, ``selector_id``, ``error_message``, IDs that would let
a stranger correlate scans, etc.). Includes the rendered intel + raw
markdown bodies so the public view can render them inline without a
second authenticated round-trip.

PublicScanReportRequest.title: PublicScanReportRequest
PublicScanReportRequest.description:
Anonymous abuse-report payload. ``contact`` is optional free text — we
do NOT require an email address; the goal is to lower the bar for users
flagging garbage. Length-capped to keep the log line readable.

PublicScanSummary.title: PublicScanSummary
PublicScanSummary.description: One row in the community feed. Strictly excludes any owner identifier.

PublicTaskResponse.title: PublicTaskResponse
PublicTaskResponse.description:
Public-safe view of a MicroserviceTask — no error_message or exit_code
stack details that could leak operator infrastructure clues.

RegistrationConfigResponse.title: RegistrationConfigResponse
RegistrationConfigResponse.description:
Public knobs the registration form needs before it can render.

``invite_code_required`` mirrors ``bool(settings.invite_code)`` so the UI
can hide the field when the backend would not enforce it anyway.

ReportSearchHit.title: ReportSearchHit
ReportSearchHit.description:
One match in the response for ``POST /api/search/reports``.

``score`` is cosine similarity in ``[-1, 1]`` for semantic
embedding matches, or a normalized lexical fallback score in
``[0, 1]`` when embeddings are unavailable. ``excerpt`` is a
~240-char window around the highest-scoring sentence, plain text so
the FE can do client-side highlighting against the query tokens.
``risk_score`` mirrors the ``ScanJobResponse`` shape so the FE can
render the same chip as the project history table.

ReportSearchRequest.title: ReportSearchRequest
ReportSearchRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/search/reports``.

``query`` is the user's plain-language description of what they
want to find ("show me anything with abuse score above 50",
"RDP exposed to the internet"). ``limit`` is an optional cap on
the number of result rows; the router enforces a hard ceiling at
:data:`_SEARCH_LIMIT_MAX` regardless of caller value.

``project_id`` is optional — when supplied the search is scoped to
that project (used by the ProjectDetailView search box). Omitted
means the global search across every project the requesting user
owns (the ``/app/search`` page).

ReportSearchResponse.title: ReportSearchResponse
ReportSearchResponse.description:
Returned by ``POST /api/search/reports``.

Always returns a (possibly empty) list — the FE renders an empty
state when no rows match. ``query`` is echoed so the FE can avoid
a stale render when the user types ahead of the in-flight request.

RescanAlertListItem.title: RescanAlertListItem
RescanAlertListItem.description:
Read-side projection of one ``rescan_alerts`` row for the
Phase-5 dashboard "Anomalous rescans" card (ticket 015).

The list endpoint joins ScanJob → Selector → Project so each row
can render without a follow-up round-trip:

* ``selector_value`` / ``selector_type`` come from the Selector
  that the parent ScanJob targeted. Both can be NULL on legacy
  rows whose Selector has been deleted (FK is ``ON DELETE SET
  NULL`` on the ScanJob side); the FE handles the empty case
  with a "(unknown)" sentinel mirroring the email body.
* ``project_name`` is from the parent ScanJob's Project.
* ``report_id`` may be NULL when the alerter inserted before the
  Report finalised, or for rows whose Report was hard-deleted.
* ``alert_message`` is a short human string — the same subject-
  line shape the email channel uses ("Anomalous change detected
  on {target}"). Computed at read time so the FE doesn't need
  to know the alerter's copy.
* ``status`` reflects the lifecycle column added in 0051;
  ``delivered_at`` (NULL = queued/failed) is preserved for the
  FE's "Sent" / "Pending" / "Failed" pill.

RescanAlertResponse.title: RescanAlertResponse
RescanAlertResponse.description:
Read-side projection of one ``rescan_alerts`` row.

``delivered_at`` NULL means "queued / failed" — the FE renders a
yellow pill. A populated timestamp renders the green "Sent" pill.
``selector_value`` is joined off the parent ScanJob so the recent-
alerts widget can render the target without a second round-trip.

RescanAlertUpdate.title: RescanAlertUpdate
RescanAlertUpdate.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/rescan-alerts/{id}`` (ticket 015).

Only ``status`` moves on this surface; ``dismissed_at`` is a
derived stamp the router manages — set to ``utcnow()`` on a
transition to ``DISMISSED``, cleared on the transition back to
``OPEN``. Clients cannot write ``dismissed_at`` directly.

ResetPasswordRequest.title: ResetPasswordRequest
ResetPasswordRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/auth/reset``.

``token`` is the raw URL-safe value handed to the user via email; the
server hashes it and looks the row up by hash.

RunnerDetail.title: RunnerDetail
RunnerDetail.description:
Full runner descriptor for ``GET /api/runners/{name}`` — adds the
Incus ``cwd`` and ``capture_paths`` operators may want to know.

RunnerOutputFile.title: RunnerOutputFile
RunnerOutputFile.description: One captured file from the runner, base64-encoded for transport.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: Seconds before the runner is killed. Dispatcher clamps to [1, 300]; omit to use the dispatcher's 60s default.

RunnerRunResponse.title: RunnerRunResponse
RunnerRunResponse.description:
Envelope returned by ``POST /api/runners/{name}/run``.

Matches ``runner_dispatch.run`` (see ``rpc.py:163-170``). Errors are
surfaced in-band: ``returncode == -1`` plus a ``kind`` field
(``unknown`` / ``invalid_args`` / ``timeout`` / ``binary_missing`` /
``render_failed``). AMQP / network failures bubble up as 502 / 503
in the route — they don't reach this envelope.

RunnerSummary.title: RunnerSummary
RunnerSummary.description:
Compact runner descriptor for ``GET /api/runners`` lists.

Mirrors the dispatcher's ``list_runners()`` shape so the route can
pass the dict through without per-field renames.

RunnerWebformField.title: RunnerWebformField
RunnerWebformField.description:
One arg slot on a runner's webform schema, as returned by
``runner_dispatch.list_runners()``.

RunnersHealthResponse.title: RunnersHealthResponse
RunnersHealthResponse.description:
Body of ``GET /api/health/runners``.

``reachable`` is the only field guaranteed to be present; the rest
come from the dispatcher's ``health()`` payload when AMQP is up.

ScamConversationArtifactCreateRequest.title: ScamConversationArtifactCreateRequest
ScamConversationArtifactCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/scam-conversations/{cid}/artifacts``.

``kind`` selects the parser branch; ``label`` is an optional
human-readable name (defaults to "(no label)" when omitted);
``body`` is the verbatim artifact text. Length cap mirrors the
BEC artifact validator so analysts can paste the same blob into
either feature.

ScamConversationArtifactResponse.title: ScamConversationArtifactResponse
ScamConversationArtifactResponse.description: One artifact row attached to a conversation.

ScamConversationCreateRequest.title: ScamConversationCreateRequest
ScamConversationCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/scam-conversations``.

``title`` is required and bounded so the conversation list view
stays scannable. Artifacts are uploaded via a separate endpoint
(one artifact per request) so the body shape stays predictable.

ScamConversationDetailResponse.title: ScamConversationDetailResponse
ScamConversationDetailResponse.description:
Full conversation shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

Includes every artifact, every finding, every entity, the most
recent synthesized brief + packet, and the suggested selector
list so a fresh F5 page load renders the conversation without a
follow-up call.

ScamConversationEntityResponse.title: ScamConversationEntityResponse
ScamConversationEntityResponse.description:
One synthesized entity row.

``kind`` is the discriminator the FE keys table grouping on
(participant / handle / url / domain / wallet / ...).

ScamConversationFindingResponse.title: ScamConversationFindingResponse
ScamConversationFindingResponse.description:
One synthesized finding row.

``kind`` is the discriminator the FE keys table grouping on
(``timeline`` / ``pressure_tactic`` / ``money_ask`` / ``script``).

ScamConversationRunSelectedSelectorsRequ.title: ScamConversationRunSelectedSelectorsRequest
ScamConversationRunSelectedSelectorsRequ.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/scam-conversations/{cid}/run-selectors``.

Sends the suggested selectors the analyst ticked back into the
project's normal selector pipeline. Capped at 10 entries to bound
the per-click ScanJob fan-out; matches the synthesizer's own
``_MAX_SUGGESTED_SELECTORS``. Per the ticket, only domain / IP /
URL / FQDN selectors are accepted here — wallets and phone
numbers stay as structured evidence and the router rejects them
with a 400.

ScamConversationSuggestedSelector.title: ScamConversationSuggestedSelector
ScamConversationSuggestedSelector.description:
One Surf candidate the analyzer recommends.

Mirrors :class:`SelectorCreate`'s shape so the FE can post the
candidates straight into the existing selector-creation endpoint
without a translation layer. Wallets and phone numbers stay as
structured evidence (per the ticket) and are NOT proposed here.

ScamConversationSummaryResponse.title: ScamConversationSummaryResponse
ScamConversationSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project conversation list.

ScanJobHistoryItem.title: ScanJobHistoryItem
ScanJobHistoryItem.description: Compact row for Surf Selector request history.

SelectorBreakdownChild.title: SelectorBreakdownChild
SelectorBreakdownChild.description:
One scannable child selector to promote from the parent.

``selector_type`` must be one of the canonical types
(Domain / FQDN / IP / URL / EmailHeaders). ``value`` is the raw
string that will land in the new ``Selector.value`` column —
already normalized by the worker, no re-classification on the
WebApp side.

SelectorBreakdownComponent.title: SelectorBreakdownComponent
SelectorBreakdownComponent.description:
One ``{kind, value}`` pair to record on the parent selector.

Embedded inside :class:`SelectorInternalBreakdownRequest`. Kept
deliberately minimal — the worker is the source of truth for
which kinds exist; the DB stores them verbatim.

SelectorBulkProjectUpdateRequest.title: SelectorBulkProjectUpdateRequest
SelectorBulkProjectUpdateRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/selectors/bulk`` (workspace IA v3 §11).

``project_id`` is the destination Project for every selector in
``selector_ids``. ``None`` moves the listed selectors to
"unassigned" (``project_id IS NULL``); a non-NULL int moves them
under that Project. Any selector whose owner does not match the
caller fails the whole request with 403 (no partial commit).

SelectorBulkProjectUpdateResponse.title: SelectorBulkProjectUpdateResponse
SelectorBulkProjectUpdateResponse.description:
Response body for ``PATCH /api/selectors/bulk``.

``updated_count`` is the number of rows the single ``UPDATE``
actually changed. The FE uses it to render the toast copy
("*N* selectors moved to *<project>*").

SelectorCandidate.title: SelectorCandidate
SelectorCandidate.description:
One LLM-extracted selector candidate.

Detector-canonical: ``value`` is whatever ``app.detect.classify``
returned for the model's raw output (lowercased hostnames, stripped
surrounding whitespace, etc.) and ``selector_type`` is the type
classify() emitted — NOT the type the model claimed. The FE renders
the type chip directly off this field.

SelectorComponentResponse.title: SelectorComponentResponse
SelectorComponentResponse.description:
One structured part of a decomposed selector (PR #2).

Emitted by MS79_SelectorBreakdown via the
``/api/internal/selectors/{id}/breakdown`` endpoint. Each row
captures one decomposed piece — ``scheme=https``, ``port=8443``,
``query-param:invite_code=XYZABC``, etc. — that the FE renders in
the breakdown panel.

SelectorExtractRequest.title: SelectorExtractRequest
SelectorExtractRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/selectors/extract``.

``prompt`` is the user's plain-language description of what they
want to investigate. ``project_id`` is optional context — it isn't
used for routing today (the endpoint is stateless and never
mutates the DB), but accepting it keeps the future option open of
biasing extraction toward selectors related to the project's
existing assets.

SelectorExtractResponse.title: SelectorExtractResponse
SelectorExtractResponse.description:
Returned by ``POST /api/selectors/extract``.

Always returns a (possibly empty) list — the FE renders an empty
state when no candidates passed validation. The endpoint NEVER
auto-adds candidates to a project; the user must confirm in the
UI and each confirmed candidate is then inserted via the existing
selector-add path.

SelectorImportResponse.title: SelectorImportResponse
SelectorImportResponse.description:
Response body for ``POST /api/projects/{id}/selectors/import``.

The endpoint regex-extracts URLs (and bare hostnames / IPs) from
an uploaded text-shaped file, dedupes against the project's
existing selectors, and inserts the new ones. The response gives
the FE everything it needs to render the post-upload result panel:

* ``imported`` — count of new selectors persisted to the DB.
* ``duplicates`` — count of regex-extracted URLs that already
  existed in the project (skipped silently — the file may legally
  list a URL twice across multiple feeds).
* ``invalid`` — count of regex hits that did not survive
  validation (empty after trailing-punct strip, no host
  component, classify() raised, etc.).
* ``source_filename`` — sanitized basename of the upload, echoed
  back so the FE can render "Imported 47 from <file>".
* ``imported_selectors`` — full ``SelectorResponse`` for each new
  row so the FE can prepend them to the table without an extra
  round-trip to ``GET /api/projects/{id}/selectors``.

SelectorInternalBreakdownRequest.title: SelectorInternalBreakdownRequest
SelectorInternalBreakdownRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/internal/selectors/{id}/breakdown``.

Bundles the two storage seams MS79 writes through on every
successful breakdown:

* ``components`` — structured parts (scheme, host, port, path,
  query-param:<name>, fragment, email-domain, network,
  prefix-length, ...). Idempotent via the
  ``uq_selector_components_selector_kind_value`` unique key.
* ``children`` — selectors worth promoting (the FQDN, the apex
  domain, the email's @-side). Each lands as a new Selector
  with ``parent_selector_id`` set to the request's path param;
  duplicates within this request and against existing children
  are silently merged on ``(parent_selector_id, value)``.

Both lists may be empty — a raw IPv4, for instance, has no
breakdown and submits ``{"components": [], "children": []}``.

SelectorInternalResolvedIpsRequest.title: SelectorInternalResolvedIpsRequest
SelectorInternalResolvedIpsRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/internal/selectors/{id}/resolved-ips``.

Emitted by MS80_SelectorExpansion after resolving a hostname to
every IP it answers with (A + AAAA + getaddrinfo flavors). Each
entry lands as both a ``selector_components`` row (audit) and a
child Selector with ``selector_type=IP`` (scannable). Idempotent
on the component UQ and ``(parent_selector_id, value)``.

Empty ``ips`` is a valid no-op (NXDOMAIN — the endpoint still
returns 200 with empty added arrays so the worker has a stable
contract).

SelectorInternalTagsRequest.title: SelectorInternalTagsRequest
SelectorInternalTagsRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/internal/selectors/{id}/tags``.

Microservice-internal endpoint — bearer-equivalent gating via the
``X-Internal-Token`` header. Carries the list of tag names a
classifier (MS78_SelectorTagging) wants attached to the selector.
Names are lowercased + upserted under the selector's
``owner_user_id`` and attached with ``selector_tags.auto = True``
so the auto-vs-manual filter on the FE keeps working.

Empty list is a valid no-op (selector value didn't match any
classifier rule — the endpoint still returns 200 with the
unchanged tag set so the caller has a stable contract).

SelectorResolvedIp.title: SelectorResolvedIp
SelectorResolvedIp.description:
One IP that MS80_SelectorExpansion resolved for a hostname.

``family`` is ``"ipv4"`` or ``"ipv6"`` — controls which
``selector_components.kind`` the row lands under
(``resolved-ip-v4`` vs ``resolved-ip-v6``).

``source`` is a short slug naming which resolver flavor surfaced
this IP — ``getaddrinfo`` for the system resolver path,
``dns-a`` / ``dns-aaaa`` for the explicit dnspython queries. Kept
as free-form text so a future resolver (DoH, Quad9-only, etc.)
can add itself without a schema change.

SelectorResponse.title: SelectorResponse
SelectorResponse.description:
Single-Selector read shape returned by every selector list / get
endpoint.

``tag_ids`` and ``tags`` carry the per-Selector tag assignments
added in ticket 010. Both fields are always present — empty
arrays when no tags are attached — so the FE can render the
column / chips against a stable shape regardless of assignment
state. ``tags`` is the parallel ``TagResponse[]`` so the FE can
render chips (which need names, not just ids) without a per-row
round-trip back to ``GET /api/tags``.

SelectorTagsPatch.title: SelectorTagsPatch
SelectorTagsPatch.description:
Body fragment for ``PATCH /api/selectors/{id}`` tag mutation.

Mirrors :class:`SelectorTagsUpdateRequest`'s shape so the
top-level PATCH can route through the same idempotent
add/remove plumbing the per-selector ``/tags`` endpoint uses.
Both fields default to empty lists so the FE can omit them.

SelectorTagsUpdateRequest.title: SelectorTagsUpdateRequest
SelectorTagsUpdateRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/selectors/{id}/tags`` (ticket 010).

``add`` is a heterogenous list:
    * ``int`` entries are existing Tag ids — looked up under the
      caller's owner scope; foreign / unknown ids 403 the whole
      request (no partial commit).
    * ``str`` entries are raw tag names — normalised lowercase and
      idempotently upserted via the ``(owner_user_id, name)``
      unique key from ticket 004 (returning the existing row if
      the name already exists). Type-and-Enter on the chips picker
      flows through this path.

``remove`` is ids only — the FE always knows the id of a chip it's
deleting. An id that isn't currently on the selector is a no-op
(does not 404), but a foreign id still 403s.

SelectorTopLevelCreate.title: SelectorTopLevelCreate
SelectorTopLevelCreate.description:
Body for ``POST /api/selectors`` (v3 — workspace IA v3 §9.2).

The top-level create accepts an optional ``project_id`` so the
Selectors page's "Add selector" form can park new rows under a
specific Project or under "no project" (NULL → unassigned). The
legacy per-Project endpoint at
``POST /api/projects/{pid}/selectors`` continues to work
unchanged for back-compat.

``selector_type`` is optional — when omitted the backend
auto-detects via the same ``classify()`` helper the legacy
endpoint uses. ``notes`` is the free-form analyst note attached
to the row at creation time.

SelectorTopLevelPatch.title: SelectorTopLevelPatch
SelectorTopLevelPatch.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/selectors/{id}`` (v3 — workspace IA v3 §9.2).

Every field is optional — the FE patches whichever fields
changed. ``project_id`` accepts ``None`` to detach a Selector
from its current Project (move to "unassigned"); a non-NULL int
moves it under the named Project (which the caller must own).
``status`` rolls through the existing enum. ``tags`` reuses the
existing add/remove discipline — see :class:`SelectorTagsPatch`.

At least one field must be set; an empty body 400s so the FE
surfaces a clear error rather than silently no-op'ing.

TagCreate.title: TagCreate
TagCreate.description: Name is normalised to lowercase by the server on every write.

TagListItem.title: TagListItem
TagListItem.description:
List shape with ``selector_count`` rollup.

``selector_count`` is the number of Selectors that carry this Tag.
Computed on read by ``GET /api/tags`` via a single grouped
aggregate — no denormalised column on ``tags`` itself in v1.

TagResponse.title: TagResponse
TagResponse.description: Single-Tag read shape returned by POST / GET / PATCH.

TierFeature.title: TierFeature
TierFeature.description: One row in a tier's ✅/❌ feature checklist.

TranslatedSegmentResponse.title: TranslatedSegmentResponse
TranslatedSegmentResponse.description:
One segment-level translation row.

Source text is preserved beside the translation per the ticket's
"keep source text beside translated text" guardrail. Confidence is
a 0-100 integer; ``uncertainty_note`` is the analyst-facing
explanation for ambiguous phrases.

TranslationArtifactCreateRequest.title: TranslationArtifactCreateRequest
TranslationArtifactCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/translations/{jid}/artifacts``.

``kind`` selects the segmenter branch; ``label`` is an optional
human-readable name; ``body`` is the verbatim text. ``source_lang_hint``
is an optional ISO 639-1 code the analyst sets when they already know
the language. ``source_document_id`` lets the analyst translate an
existing project document instead of pasting (the router copies the
document body into ``body`` before persisting).

TranslationArtifactResponse.title: TranslationArtifactResponse
TranslationArtifactResponse.description: One artifact row attached to a job.

TranslationJobCreateRequest.title: TranslationJobCreateRequest
TranslationJobCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/translations``.

``title`` is required and bounded so the job-list view stays
scannable. Artifacts are uploaded via a separate endpoint (one per
request) so the body shape stays predictable.

TranslationJobDetailResponse.title: TranslationJobDetailResponse
TranslationJobDetailResponse.description:
Full job shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

Includes every artifact, every segment, every entity, and the
synthesized bookkeeping (summary markdown, model + tokens,
suggested selectors). One round-trip is enough to render the page.

TranslationJobSummaryResponse.title: TranslationJobSummaryResponse
TranslationJobSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project translation-job list.

TranslationRunSelectorsRequest.title: TranslationRunSelectorsRequest
TranslationRunSelectorsRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/translations/{jid}/run-selectors``.

Capped at 10 entries to bound the per-click ``Selector`` fan-out;
matches the synthesizer's own cap. Only network IOC kinds
(``Domain`` / ``URL`` / ``EmailHeaders``) are accepted — names,
handles, organizations, etc. are review-only.

TranslationSuggestedSelector.title: TranslationSuggestedSelector
TranslationSuggestedSelector.description:
One Surf candidate the translator recommends.

Mirrors :class:`SelectorCreate`'s shape so the FE can post the
candidates straight into the existing selector-creation pipeline
without a translation layer.

TriageChildResponse.title: TriageChildResponse
TriageChildResponse.description:
One child Surf row inside a triage detail response.

Mirrors the smallest subset of ``ScanJobResponse`` the triage UI
needs to render the per-IOC pill list and the public-slug link to
the underlying OFIR.

TriageDetailResponse.title: TriageDetailResponse
TriageDetailResponse.description:
Returned by ``GET /api/triage/{id}``.

The ``summary_markdown`` field is populated only after every child
Surf has hit a terminal status AND the meta-summary LLM call has
completed. Until then the FE polls / streams via the existing
scan-progress channel and renders per-IOC pills.

TriageHistoryItem.title: TriageHistoryItem
TriageHistoryItem.description: Compact row for Alert Triage request history.

TriageReviewedSelector.title: TriageReviewedSelector
TriageReviewedSelector.description: One analyst-reviewed selector to run from a triage request.

TriageStartResponse.title: TriageStartResponse
TriageStartResponse.description:
Returned by ``POST /api/triage`` once extract + kick-off finish.

``extracted_iocs`` echoes the validated bag (so the UI can render
pills immediately for hashes/emails too). ``started_scan_job_ids``
is the list of fan-out child Surf ids — the UI uses these to start
polling per-child status without waiting on the GET.

TriageSubmitRequest.title: TriageSubmitRequest
TriageSubmitRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/triage``.

The free-form text is whatever the analyst pasted — alert email
body, Suricata log line, raw Slack message, etc. We cap it at
50k chars so a runaway client can't post a 10 MB block to chew
LLM cost; the hard byte cap also keeps the prompt budget sane
on the Haiku call.

UpdateMeRequest.title: UpdateMeRequest
UpdateMeRequest.description:
Update the current user's email and/or password.

``current_password`` is required for any field change.

UserInviteCodeResponse.title: UserInviteCodeResponse
UserInviteCodeResponse.description:
List/create response for a per-user invite code.

The plaintext ``code`` is included on every list — invite codes are not
long-lived auth secrets, just one-shot signup gates, and the inviter
needs to be able to re-copy the value to share with a friend. We
intentionally do **not** expose ``used_by_user_id``: knowing whether a
code was claimed is fine; knowing **who** claimed it is a privacy
leak we don't need to ship.

UserPreferencesResponse.title: UserPreferencesResponse
UserPreferencesResponse.description:
Read-side view of the per-user notification toggles.

v1 ships exactly one toggle (``alert_on_anomalous_rescan``); future
notification opt-outs (digest emails, weekly summaries, etc.) land
on the same model so the Account → Notifications panel keeps a
single round-trip.

UserPreferencesUpdate.title: UserPreferencesUpdate
UserPreferencesUpdate.description:
Body for ``PUT /api/account/preferences``.

Every field is optional — callers PATCH-style only the toggles they
want to change. We don't fork to PATCH because the URL is a bag of
flags rather than a sub-resource and a single shape is easier to
keep aligned with the FE store.

VerifyEmailRequest.title: VerifyEmailRequest
VerifyEmailRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/auth/verify``.

Same shape contract as :class:`ResetPasswordRequest` — the raw
URL-safe token from the email, hashed server-side and looked up
against ``email_verification_tokens``.

VictimReportArtifactCreateRequest.title: VictimReportArtifactCreateRequest
VictimReportArtifactCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/victim-reports/{rid}/artifacts``.

``kind`` selects the (future) parser branch; ``label`` is an
optional human-readable name; ``body`` is the verbatim artifact
text. Length cap mirrors the scam-conversation artifact validator.

VictimReportArtifactResponse.title: VictimReportArtifactResponse
VictimReportArtifactResponse.description: One artifact row attached to a victim report.

VictimReportCreateRequest.title: VictimReportCreateRequest
VictimReportCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/victim-reports``.

``title`` is required and bounded so the report list view stays
scannable. The ticket allows ``raw text plus optional artifact
references`` on create -- we honour that by accepting an optional
initial artifact (``initial_body`` + ``initial_kind`` +
``initial_label``) so the FE's "paste your story, click submit"
flow is one round-trip. Subsequent artifacts are uploaded via the
artifacts endpoint.

VictimReportDetailResponse.title: VictimReportDetailResponse
VictimReportDetailResponse.description:
Full report shape returned by the GET-by-id endpoint.

Includes every artifact, every finding, every entity, the most
recent synthesized narrative + packet, and the suggested-selector
list so a fresh F5 page load renders the report without a
follow-up call.

VictimReportFindingResponse.title: VictimReportFindingResponse
VictimReportFindingResponse.description:
One synthesized finding row.

``kind`` is the discriminator the FE keys table grouping on
(``timeline`` / ``loss_item`` / ``missing_info``).

VictimReportRunSelectedSelectorsRequest.title: VictimReportRunSelectedSelectorsRequest
VictimReportRunSelectedSelectorsRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/projects/{pid}/victim-reports/{rid}/run-selectors``.

Sends the suggested selectors the analyst ticked back into the
project's normal selector pipeline. Capped at 10 entries to bound
the per-click ScanJob fan-out; matches the normalizer's own
``_MAX_SUGGESTED_SELECTORS``. Per the ticket, only domain / IP /
URL / FQDN selectors are accepted here -- wallets, phone numbers,
bank details, and names stay as structured evidence and the
router rejects them with a 400.

VictimReportSuggestedSelector.title: VictimReportSuggestedSelector
VictimReportSuggestedSelector.description:
One Surf candidate the normalizer recommends.

Mirrors :class:`SelectorCreate`'s shape so the FE can post the
candidates straight into the existing selector-creation endpoint
without a translation layer. Wallets, phone numbers, bank details,
and names stay structured-evidence-only (per the ticket) and are
NOT proposed here.

VictimReportSummaryResponse.title: VictimReportSummaryResponse
VictimReportSummaryResponse.description: One row in the per-project victim-report listing.

WebhookCreatedResponse.title: WebhookCreatedResponse
WebhookCreatedResponse.description: Returned ONCE on creation. ``secret`` is the only chance to see it.

WebhookResponse.title: WebhookResponse
WebhookResponse.description: List/get response — never includes the plaintext secret.
